content.text:
Current internal scene model contains no identified colors or shapes for any object; all color and shape distributions are flat/missing.

Active selection:
- View A: attention is almost certainly on the lower location (selection probability 0.9997). The other three locations have near-zero current selection.
- View B: attention is almost certainly on the left location (selection probability 0.99994). Other locations are effectively unselected.

Recoverability (chance to access that object's information) declines with time/steps without resampling. For the currently attended items:
- A lower: recoverability now ≈ 0.629, after one step ≈ 0.459, after two ≈ 0.336.
- B left: now ≈ 0.451, after one ≈ 0.333, after two ≈ 0.253.
Other locations have lower recoverabilities (listed in the model).

Predicted effects of redirecting attention:
- In View A, issuing a command naming a location reliably shifts predicted selection to that named location (e.g., command "upper" → upper ≈ 0.999; "right" → right ≈ 0.999; "left" → left ≈ 0.999; "lower" preserves lower ≈ 0.9997). Thus A is under strong control.
- In View B, predicted selections are largely concentrated on left now and commands do not uniquely steer selection to a single alternative (the model predicts high probabilities for multiple locations under different commands), so control is limited/ambiguous.
